approvals.reason: The installer binds error hooks and the one worker message receiver on the active self shim, including a fresh test realm; it does not execute requests. The receiver alone validates protocol and requested features, awaits the shared census gate, then synchronously dispatches the request and classifies failures by source. Folding them into one entry would remove the explicit reinstallation seam needed by existing worker tests or duplicate registration. They have distinct call/timing responsibilities and a single implementation of each in the same owner module.

The residential porch is a bounded doorway target immediately outside a house footprint, and is used by commuteHumanToBuilding to set indoorBuildingId and enable legitimate sleep. The venue arc deliberately spreads social visitors much farther south of a building without signaling arrival at home. Combining these would place residents at audience distances or make leisure crowds converge on a door. Both are pure read-only calculations in the same humanMovement owner; the regression explicitly pins their different geometry and the leader-spouse arrival contract.

Distinct lifecycle contracts: discardSpotlightReturn intentionally invalidates a previous-colony camera/pause snapshot on load without returning or restoring it, whereas takeSpotlightReturn atomically returns the prior snapshot once on ordinary scene completion. They share the necessary clear operation but differ in returned values, callers, timing, and session-safety behavior; combining into a single ambiguous call would risk restoring prior colony controls. The test verifies both one-shot consume and discard-on-load semantics.

Both are thin validated field setters that delegate the shared state rewrite to setValidatedOption. Workshop requires a known recipe id and a Workshop target; hunting prey requires a known prey id and a HuntingSpot target. They write different persisted fields, refuse different invalid inputs, and are invoked by different worker operations; merging them would lose the typed command surface. Regressions cover both command round-trips and no-op identity.

The residence-occupant rule counts only player-owned settlers (and cursed Moon Howlers with no faction) for beds and rosters; the settler-relationship rule accepts any living human of any faction, and a cursed werewolf regardless of faction, for the relationship record (invariants, lifecycle cleanup, humanTick), never for bed occupancy. Merging them would either seat visitors and rivals in beds or drop foreign settlers from relationship restoration. They are distinct predicates with different consumers and faction rules.

Two disjoint age windows with different contracts: youth love is the 12-17 band (YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE, minor, gender required, no courtship cooldown) while courtship is 18+ (adult, lifespan cap, cooldown). They share the necessary available-single conditions (alive, player, no partner, single status, no youth partner, not pregnant, not imprisoned), but merging would either admit minors to courtship or block youth love. Each has its own gate, and the handoff from youth love to courtship is pinned separately.

Both accessors derive the same passability rules using buildPathGrid, but their cache owners and side effects are intentionally different. getPathGrid feeds the active simulation and records rebuilds; its identity changes cause setCurrentPathMap to invalidate movement waypoint caches. getReadOnlyPathGrid serves the UI/logistics projection with an independent cache and no simulation metrics or waypoint invalidation. Combining their cache state would let render snapshots invalidate live movement routes. The logistics-overlay regression proves separate grid/buffer identities and unchanged simulation cache identity after a projection read; the terrain pathfinding test separately exercises the simulation cache.

getRecentFoodFlow is the canonical bounded contiguous-history measurement and retains raw all-spend reporting, with an optional meals-only consumption projection for sustainable growth. getProjectedFoodSupply calls that reader and then forecasts future meal needs from the historical consumption slope, rather than duplicating the history scan. The first returns retrospective measured production and consumption; the second computes risk against future population. Merging them would conflate measured accounting with forward demand and lose the separate caller contracts. Tests cover both modes and the one-off recruitment expense regression.

These functions concern unrelated domains with different inputs and outputs. getProjectedFoodSupply reads completed food-ledger history and reports a predicted daily need, while getCaravanMoveTarget computes a caravan's physical movement destination based on its trade-route journey. Their token similarity is accidental shared array/math operations; they have different simulation owners, timing and data dependencies. Existing regressions cover food-flow projections and caravan route progression separately.

loadNames is the cached public entry; the async body it assigns to loadPromise is the implementation it awaits. There is one implementation, not two: the outer function owns the ready check and single-flight cache, the inner promise runs disk, raw-import and fetch fallbacks once.

Both scan a contiguous entity array within one radius, but their contracts differ. forEachInArrayRadius is a visitor: it reports every living entity inside the radius, counts each candidate for the spatial metrics, and stops only when the callback returns false (the child playmate cap relies on that). naiveFindClosestInArray answers one nearest-match query: it takes a distance-aware predicate, keeps the best distance so far, drops later-but-farther matches before counting them, and returns one entity or undefined. Merging them would either give the visitor a nearest-match return it never uses or make the nearest scan report candidates nobody asked for. No writes in either.

Both strip replica-held fields from a tick delta by delegating to stripCoveredEntityFields, but their coverage contracts differ. Relationship coverage is revision-exact: a map ships again only when its revision changes. Profile coverage also stores a tick stamp and re-ships once PROFILE_REFRESH_TICKS elapses, so a missed writer can only be briefly stale. Merging them would either drop that refresh window or re-ship relationship maps on a timer nobody asked for. Both are write-free over the delta.

These are domain-distinct grid projections despite identical integer tile indexing. beautyAt reads decorative visual influence and returns a numeric score (0 off-map); isGroundWalkableAt reads physical collision occupancy and returns a boolean, treating absent/off-map grids as non-blocking for legacy movement recovery and allowing non-solid scenery. Neither mutates game state. Combining them would make ambient beauty a collision authority or force a generic grid value abstraction, violating their separate owners. Tests cover beauty scoring and path obstruction separately.

Thin adapters over the one placement decision owner getPlaceBuildingFailureReason: canPlaceBuilding returns its boolean for the command path, canPlaceBuildingSnapshot returns the same verdict for the renderer. They delegate to the single decision and exist only to keep the boolean surface; merging them into the owner would duplicate the boolean rule.

Fixed-layout render-buffer accessors generated from one row contract: each reads a distinct word of the same slot (id, type code, position, velocity, sprite fields, flags, hunt slot, residence id, energy). The typed reader exists so no caller re-derives offsets; collapsing them would remove that single offset owner. Regressions exercise the packed buffer through the real worker boundary.

Re-entrancy wrapper versus the attempt body: start() coalesces concurrent callers and owns the startPromise lifecycle, while the local async body performs unlock/play/fallback with a generation guard. Folding them would either lose the re-entrancy contract or duplicate the generation checks.

Unrelated loops that both scan a bounded number of candidate points: the wildlife spawner draws passable ground from the yearly-event stream, the chronicle anchor resolves a settlement centre. No shared rule, data or owner; the similarity is the loop shape only.

Distinct predicates for distinct building classes: findStaffedHotels returns completed player Hotels with a posted hotelier (lodging capacity), listPlayerResidences returns completed player residences (bed accounting). They share only the completed-player filter and are consumed by different services; merging them would put a staffing rule inside the housing census.

Parallel but separate staffing rules: a Hotel needs its hotelier posted to lodge guests, a Hospital needs a doctor on shift to treat patients. Different job types, different service owners. The shared shape is the completed-player-building check, already delegated to the building owner.

One shared download helper plus three format writers (JSON, CSV, text). The formats differ in MIME type, escaping and column layout; the shared helper owns the anchor/blob/revoke lifecycle. Collapsing the three would lose the player-facing format choice, which the log panel now exports over the full stored set.
